name: Hawk Ridge
description: Hawk Ridge is a stark, angular world of rust-colored rock and deep canyons, where tectonic forces have thrust up mountain ranges in parallel ridges that stripe the planet like the ribs of some buried leviathan. The thin atmosphere supports wispy clouds of ice crystals at high altitude, and the sky shifts from pale salmon at the horizon to near-black at the zenith. Canyon systems between the ridges plunge to depths where the thin air thickens enough to support hardy microbial colonies in sheltered alcoves.

The wind on Hawk Ridge is constant but thin, more felt as a gentle pressure than heard as sound. Dust devils spiral across the canyon floors with a lazy grace, and the temperature drops precipitously in the shadow of the ridges, where frost forms on rock faces even at equatorial latitudes. The landscape has a monumental quality, every vista dominated by the repeating pattern of ridge and canyon extending to the curved horizon, like the terrain itself was designed by a mind fond of parallel lines.

Ancient ruins occupy several of the highest ridge crests, their foundations carved directly into the bedrock with a precision that suggests either advanced technology or immense patience. The structures are roofless and minimal, more framework than architecture, as if designed for a species that valued exposure to the sky above shelter from the elements. No artifacts have been recovered from the sites, only the bare stone frameworks, leading some researchers to theorize that the builders took everything when they departed.

Hawk Ridge's mineral deposits are commercially viable but unremarkable, and the planet's primary draw is archaeological. The ridge-crest ruins represent a unique architectural tradition found nowhere else in surveyed space, and the question of who built them and why they chose this windswept world drives ongoing research. Funding is sporadic and conditions are harsh, and the thin atmosphere limits operational time for unsuited personnel. Hawk Ridge keeps its secrets behind walls of cold thin air and endless ridges marching toward the horizon.
